content: I'll read the test image and the part index file at the same time.

The test image shows a tomato stem cut open longitudinally, revealing extensive brown/tan discoloration of the internal vascular/pith tissue throughout the stem. The outer green tissue remains intact. This is clearly a stem disease with internal vascular browning.

From the part index, this is a **stem** symptom. Candidates: Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers, Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato, Bacterial_Wilt, Verticillium_Wilt, etc.

The internal brown vascular discoloration visible when stem is cut lengthwise is specifically described for **Verticillium_Wilt** and **Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato**. I'll use my reference view on Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato since the image shows pith browning throughout the stem.

The reference image for Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato (bottom left, image 5606081) shows a stem being cut open with brown internal pith discoloration — matching the test image well. The test image shows a Y-shaped forked stem cut longitudinally with the entire interior pith turned brown/tan, while the outer green tissue remains intact. This is highly characteristic of Bacterial Canker (Clavibacter michiganensis), where the pith turns brown and necrotic.

Verticillium Wilt would show lighter streaking rather than the uniform, extensive brown pith seen here. The complete interior pith browning is the hallmark of Bacterial Canker.
